expectedTruths: Population (standardised common factors): BI = 0.28 PE + 0.03 EE + 0.12 SI + 0.08 FC + 0.18 HM + 0.27 HT; USE = 0.35 BI + 0.12 FC + 0.22 HT. The six predictors are correlated 0.25-0.45 (population.json exogenousCorrelations). R^2 — BI 0.450080, USE 0.308296.

EE -> BI is near zero by design (0.03): its unique effect is negligible although corr(EE, BI) = 0.366000 in the population, because EE correlates with PE, FC and HM. With N = 450 its bootstrap confidence interval is expected to include 0: the example teaches a non-significant hypothesis test. FC -> BI (0.08) is small and may or may not be significant in a sample.
For every estimate and bootstrap draw: total effect = direct + indirect effect (recursive linear model identity).
Agreement profiles differ by construct (EE high-agreement; PE and FC mild-agreement; HT and USE low-agreement; others symmetric).
Sample estimates on 7-point items are compared engine-to-engine; the population values are approached only approximately (discretisation, sampling error and, for classic PLS, attenuation).
